האחורי אומר שחור אם מספר השחורים שלפניו אי־זוגי ולבן אם הוא זוגי. כל הבא משלב את הזוגיות עם הצבעים שכבר נשמעו ועם מה שהוא רואה, ונשאר רק כובעו. כך n−1 יודעים בוודאות. אי אפשר להבטיח גם לראשון לדעת, כי כובעו אינו משפיע על שום מידע שיש לו.

The rear dwarf announces parity of black hats ahead. Each later dwarf XORs that message with correctly announced colors and visible hats, leaving their own color. Thus n−1 know with certainty. The first cannot know, because flipping only their invisible hat changes none of their observations.

For 50, use pairs:one says the next hat and the partner repeats it. For 98, two first speakers encode red/blue parities of the other 98. For 99, the first says the sum modulo 3 of visible color codes;each later speaker subtracts visible and already-correct colors. All 100 cannot be guaranteed because the first cannot observe their own hat.

hints: אפשר להשתמש בתשובה שאינה בהכרח נכונה כדי לעזור למישהו שרואים לפני הדובר. איך עושים זאת בזוגות?
ל־98 האחרים אפשר להעביר שני ביטים על צבעים באמצעות שני הדוברים הראשונים. האם זוגיות של שני צבעים מספיקה לזהות את השלישי?

### Extension:100 dwarfs and three hat colors
Each of 100 dwarfs wears one of three hat colors, with repetition allowed. The source phrase saying everyone has a different color cannot literally mean 100 distinct colors chosen from three. Design prior-agreed strategies guaranteeing at least 50 correct answers, then at least 98, and finally at least 99. Prove each guarantee and whether 100 can be guaranteed.

Information contract:number front 1 to rear 100. Each sees all hats ahead but not their own or behind. Speakers answer 100,99,...,1 and hear every previous reply. Each reply is one of the three color names and is scored as that speaker own-hat guess;no extra timing, motion or vocal channel is allowed. Color names may carry agreed codes. The last two in line are 100 and 99, the first two speakers. No counts per color are supplied.
hints: A reply that is not necessarily correct for its speaker can help someone visible ahead. How can adjacent pairs use that?
Two first speakers can send two bits about the remaining 98 hats. Can parities for two colors distinguish all three possibilities?
To use just one signaler, encode colors 0,1,2 and announce a sum modulo 3. Later speakers subtract visible colors and previous answers known to be correct.
